checks.label: Extreme values in the tails distort the mean but not the median, since the median is based on ranks: slipping the ringed reading off the top of the scale lifts the mean of the fifty by a fiftieth of the slip and moves the median by half a meter step at most, at every random error

The mean will be pulled in the direction of the skewness: if the right tail is heavier than the left, the mean will be greater than the median. Insulation resistance nudged by factors makes a bell about 200 MΩ on a scale of 20 columns a decade, each 12% more than the last; on an even scale its mean sits above its median and the settled beam balances there, level, with every reading on both scales and no bead under r 3.2

From every raw data value, subtract the mean, square the results, average them over one fewer than the count and then take the square root: every SD worked on screen follows that recipe line by line and agrees with the standard deviation of its readings

Worked by hand: 0.79, 0.80, 0.80, 0.81 and 0.85 Ω add to 4.05 Ω and balance at 0.81 Ω, with 0.04 Ω of distance each side; nine readings of 0.50 Ω and one of 1.50 Ω have a mean of 0.60 Ω and a median of 0.50 Ω; 0.77 to 0.82 Ω give squares adding to 0.0016, then 0.0004 and an SD of 0.02 Ω; 0.75 to 0.83 Ω give 0.0036, 0.0009 and 0.03 Ω; sets A and B both span 0.08 Ω with SDs of 0.028 and 0.040 Ω; the bumpy and flat sets 0.016 and 0.035 Ω; the ten circuits a mean of 0.62 Ω and an SD of 0.13 Ω; twelve nudges of −½ to +½ add to an error of SD 1; halving the random error from 0.02 to 0.01 Ω takes the fifty from 10 columns to 5 and their fullest column from 11 to 20 beads; a 1.00 Ω slip lifts the mean exactly 0.02 Ω and the SD to about 0.14 Ω

Drawn true: settled, the fulcrum sits under the mean and the beam is level, honest or slipped, at every random error; a slip past the scale sits in its overflow pile, named, never clipped; no two beads touch, every bead inside its room, none under r 3.2; the values clear of every bead; the fade deepest at 3:1 and palest still seen; each puzzle accepts only its right answer, its fulcrum lands where its pick puts it, and before an answer nothing gives the answer away; every demonstration settles within 5 s, every answer within 2.5 s
